diagram_math_checks.justification: The Example defines coordinate vertices {0,...,k-1}^2 and G_k. For k=5 the figure has 25 vertices, with five horizontal and five vertical paths, each subdivided by vertices into four edges: 40 undirected nearest-neighbor edges, no diagonals or fill edges. Visual degrees are 2 at four corners, 3 at twelve other boundary vertices, 4 at nine interior vertices, totaling degree 80. All outer boundary edges are visible in standalone native capture; no named-node cycle syntax is used.

The local algorithm Definition chooses lower median floor((m-1)/2). At m=5 it selects coordinate 2 in both directions. Orange S has 5+5-1=9 vertices. Its deletion leaves B1={0,1}x{0,1}, B2={0,1}x{3,4}, B3={3,4}x{0,1}, B4={3,4}x{3,4}, disconnected in the nearest-neighbor graph. Axis i1 points right, i2 up; labels match lexicographic lower corners (0,0),(0,3),(3,0),(3,3). This is the procedure restated by local F1.

For B1 side length 2 the lower median is 0. Cyan T is exactly {(0,0),(0,1),(1,0)} and has 3 vertices. Deleting it leaves (1,1), the only child, recursively placed before T. F1 and the algorithm Definition place all four recursively ordered B boxes before S. Color carries membership only; figure asserts no factor-fill or cost relation.

Existing verification steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 are unchanged. Step 1.1 proves positive definiteness algebraically and step 2.1 specializes F2 bounds, without reference to the new figure. The Remarks expressly preserve that independent justification.
